release_name: Accessibility: a real heading, and readable provenance text
notes: First accessibility pass. The sheets came out clean and need no change: opening either the detail or the filter sheet moves focus inside it, marks the background inert - verified by trying to focus a background button and failing, not just by reading the attribute - locks page scroll, sets aria-hidden and aria-expanded correctly, closes on Escape and restores focus to the element that opened it. Also clean: every visible control has an accessible name, no image lacks alt text, landmarks and polite live regions are present, and the html lang attribute correctly follows the EN/FR toggle, which is the failure I most expected to find. Two genuine defects fixed. (1) The page had NO h1 at all - the two headings were both inside sheets - so anyone navigating by heading had no top-level landmark for the page. The brand title is now the h1, with margins reset so the layout is pixel-identical. (2) The --soft token used by the trust strip, the line that carries the data-provenance claim on every card, was #8f8178: 3.76:1 on white at 11px, below the 4.5:1 AA floor. Darkened to #7d7168, now 4.74:1, still lighter than --muted so the visual hierarchy is unchanged. One apparent third failure, the EN language button at a ratio of 1.0, was my measuring probe rather than the app: it read a translucent white overlay as opaque white when the real background is the dark maroon hero gradient. No data change: 426 rows.
